question: Not shared. P-339 detects current MoCA-defined MCI (MoCA < 26 at assessment), patient by patient, in hospitalised type 2 diabetes patients aged 40-75. P-165 predicts, visit by visit, whether an MCI diagnosis code will be recorded within one year after a primary-care visit, for Stanford Healthcare patients aged 65 or older. So the task (present detection by psychometric cut-off against a near-future recorded diagnosis), the population class (diabetic inpatients against general older primary-care patients) and the unit of analysis (patients against visits) all differ. Both use clinical tabular data, though P-165's 480 predictors include NLP concepts from clinical notes.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (match in type; the endpoints and units differ).

figures.P-339: 95% CIs as printed. Training, apparent (n = 236): 0.765 [0.705, 0.826]. Validation (n = 101; 49 MCI/52 NC): 0.690 [0.588, 0.792]. Optimism-corrected C-index 0.747 [0.695, 0.800].
figures.P-165: Random forest on the temporal test set (visits in 2020 and after): ROC-AUC 68.2 +/- 0.7 (XGBoost 66.8 +/- 0.8; logistic 57.0 +/- 1.1). The paper does not print the test-set size or define the +/-. Read as one SD, the 95% range is 0.682 +/- 1.96*0.007 = [0.668, 0.696]. The test set holds thousands of visits (the cohort has 531,387, of which 8,990 lead to an MCI diagnosis within a year), so a Hanley-McNeil interval would be no wider.

matched_figure_check: The held-out figures match on validation stage, and they agree. P-339's validation AUC 0.690 [0.588, 0.792] contains P-165's 0.682, and P-165's range [0.668, 0.696] contains 0.690. The recorded gap exists only because the record uses P-339's apparent training AUC (0.765, whose interval [0.705, 0.826] excludes 0.682). The papers' own held-out figures dissolve it.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: both AUCs are below 0.97.
reason: The papers ask different clinical questions: present MoCA-defined MCI in diabetic inpatients, against a recorded MCI diagnosis within a year of a primary-care visit in patients aged 65 or older, counted by visit (condition 1). On like-for-like held-out figures (0.690 against 0.682) they agree within uncertainty (condition 3); beyond_uncertainty is true only for the recorded apparent training AUC. The recorded disagreement rests on that training figure and on the record labelling P-165 as current detection (T1) when it predicts a future diagnosis (condition 6).

quotes.quote: Based on their Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores, participants were categorized into two groups: the normal cognition (NC) group (n = 179) and the mild cognitive impairment (MCI) group (n = 158).
with AUC values of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.705–0.826) in the training cohort and 0.690 (95% CI 0.588–0.792) in the validation cohort (Fig. 4C, D).
Our cohort include 531,387 primary care visits where the patient is 65 years or older.
was assigned with a binary label indicating if the patient has at least one MCI diagnosis code within one year follow up from the time of their primary care visit
The random forest model has a higher ROC-AUC (68.2%±0.7%) than xgboost and logistic regression models on the test set.
